Europe in 1836: Germany is 39 separate states. Italy is a patchwork of kingdoms and duchies. Two empires rule the east.

31 years later, the map is unrecognizable.

What happened in between — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The 1836 map is the world the Congress of Vienna built: designed in 1815 to freeze France, balance the powers, and suppress two dangerous new ideas — nationalism and democracy.

For 33 years, it mostly worked.

2/ Then 1848: revolution in Paris, Vienna, Berlin, Milan, Budapest — the "Springtime of Peoples."

Almost all of it was crushed within a year.

But every crowned head in Europe had now seen the future, and the smart ones decided to manage change rather than fight it.

3/ Italy moved first. Piedmont + France beat Austria in 1859; Garibaldi and 1,000 volunteers took the south in 1860.

By 1861 the patchwork was a Kingdom of Italy — minus Rome and Venice, for now.

4/ And here is 1867: Italy nearly whole, the German states consolidating around Prussia after Austria's defeat in 1866, and Austria itself forced to split power with Hungary — becoming Austria-Hungary that very year.

5/ 1836 → 1867: from 39 German states to the brink of one Germany; from 8 Italian states to one Italy.

The age of small states was over. The age of mass nation-states — and mass wars — had begun.

Follow @forummapping for more before/after maps.
